title: Field Report: jeton load_credentials mishandles token-less files — fix belongs in jeton repo (no .bon there)

brief.done: jeton loads and refreshes a token-less ADC-shaped file correctly and never writes a lossy shape back; test pinned in jeton's suite.
brief.how:
In jeton: (1) refresh condition becomes `if not creds.valid and creds.refresh_token` (covers never-had-token as well as expired); (2) _save_credentials round-trips unknown fields from the source file (read-merge-write) or gains a persist=False param callers can set for caller-owned files. Add a unit test with an ADC-shaped fixture (no token, no expiry). jeton repo has no .bon — this item lives here as jeton's main consumer; do the work in ~/repos/spm1001/jeton.

NOTE (2026-07-26 audit): hazard 2 (lossy save) was already fixed by 421abbb (2026-05-04, predates this brief) with test coverage. Remaining: the refresh condition (auth.py:97 'creds.expired' -> 'not creds.valid') + any load_credentials test at all. While there: _CANONICAL_TOKEN_FIELDS (auth.py:707) is dead code — clean deletion.

CORRECTION 2026-09-12 (review verifier): As of 2026-09-12 what remains is one line (auth.py:97 `creds.expired` -> `not creds.valid`), an ADC-shaped fixture test in tests/test_auth.py, and deleting dead `_CANONICAL_TOKEN_FIELDS` (auth.py:707); step 2 shipped in 421abbb, and step 4 (bump mise's pin) is moot because mise pins jeton to git HEAD (mise-en-space/pyproject.toml:128), so a reinstall is all mise needs.
brief.what: 1. Fix refresh condition in jeton auth.py. 2. Make save shape lossless or optional. 3. ADC-fixture unit test. 4. Bump mise's jeton dep if pinned; consider then retiring mise's guest-mode bypass or keeping it as defense-in-depth.
brief.why:
Found live 2026-06-10 under Cornichon guest mode. jeton/src/jeton/auth.py::load_credentials only refreshes when creds.expired — but google-auth reports expired=False when the file has NO expiry field, so an ADC-shaped authorized_user file (no token, no expiry) is returned as invalid -> None, misdiagnosed by callers as a revoked refresh token. Verified empirically: Credentials(token=None,...) gives expired=False, valid=False. Second hazard in the same path: the post-refresh _save_credentials writes jeton's token.json shape, silently dropping fields like type / quota_project_id / universe_domain — handed an ADC file, a successful refresh would corrupt it for any ADC consumer (e.g. an SDK reading GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS). Mise BYPASSES both in guest mode (adapters/http_client.py), but jeton itself remains wrong for any other consumer.

title: jeton exposes the listener half — serve a pre-minted auth URL's callback (mise stops hand-rolling it)

brief.done: Public jeton API serves a pre-minted URL callback and exchanges it; mise consumes it and its hand-rolled listener is deleted; both repos tests green
brief.how:
Design first: either authenticate(auth_url=...) (skip mint when given, parse expected state from the URL) or a separate listen_and_exchange(auth_url, ...). Bake in what mise's implementation learned tonight: (1) THREADED server — a single-threaded http.server wedges on Chrome's speculative second connection (seen live); (2) bind the listener BEFORE any webbrowser.open — a busy port must not burn a consent click; (3) validate state parsed from the pre-minted URL (CSRF; reject mismatches); (4) on timeout or failed exchange the persisted .pkce_state.json must SURVIVE so the --code path still works (jeton already deletes only on success — keep that); (5) headless is first-class: an ssh -L tunnel delivers callbacks, so do NOT raise HeadlessError in this mode — listen anyway, skip only the browser-open. Reference implementation to consume-and-delete: mise-en-space auth.py (_serve_pre_minted, _PreMintedCallbackHandler) + tests/unit/test_setup_oauth.py (handler CSRF tests, single-mint invariant, port semantics).

CORRECTION 2026-09-12 (review verifier): Brief is accurately priced; one detail moved under it: jeton 1.4.0 (d075bca) now keys persisted PKCE verifiers by OAuth state param (`_pkce_verify_minted`, auth.py:194), so lesson (4) — the verifier must survive a failed exchange — should be checked against the per-state file rather than a single .pkce_state.json.
brief.what: 1. Pick the API shape (param on authenticate vs new function) 2. Implement with the five lessons above 3. Tests: state validation, timeout leaves verifier intact, port-busy path 4. mise migrates — _serve_pre_minted collapses to the jeton call, hand-rolled listener + handler deleted, mise tests stay green (that swap ships as a small mise batch item, minted when actionable)
brief.why:
mise 1.3.1 (mise-zefahe, 2026-07-07) fixed the setup_oauth PKCE self-race with a single-flow split: the tool mints via jeton.get_auth_url (verifier persisted), a detached subprocess listens and exchanges via jeton.authenticate(code=...). The missing middle — run a callback listener for a URL minted elsewhere — has no public jeton API, so mise now carries ~90 lines (auth.py _serve_pre_minted + _PreMintedCallbackHandler) that near-duplicate jeton's private _auto_flow/_OAuthCallbackHandler. jeton owns the OAuth machinery; consumers shouldn't fork listeners.

title: Field Report: uv tool install jeton fails — no entry points declared

brief.why: 2026-08-07, tube, during plongeur RLD recovery: `uv tool install ~/repos/spm1001/jeton` failed with 'No executables are provided by package jeton; removing tool'. The batterie convention (uv tool install <path>) doesn't work for this package, so a session reaching for jeton on a machine without it cannot self-serve.
brief.what: Add a [project.scripts] entry point to pyproject.toml (e.g. jeton = jeton.cli:main or wherever main lives), verify uv tool install then exposes a jeton executable
brief.done: uv tool install ~/repos/spm1001/jeton succeeds on a clean machine and `jeton --help` runs
brief.how: CORRECTION 2026-09-12 (review verifier): As of 2026-09-12 this is not a one-line pyproject fix: jeton has no executable code to expose (no main/argparse anywhere in src/jeton), so `uv tool install` failing is uv correctly reporting a library. Either the item becomes 'add a minimal jeton CLI (e.g. auth/refresh/status)' or it closes as not-applicable with a note that jeton installs as a dependency (`uv add jeton@git+...`), never as a tool.
